keyVerseText: Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like as the other.
rootMeaning: The root of ὑγιής (hygiḗs) is connected to the Greek verb αὐξάνω (auxánō), meaning 'to grow' or 'to increase.' This etymology suggests that ὑγιής originally conveys a sense of growth toward wholeness or soundness, rather than merely the absence of disease. Thus, the word carries a dynamic sense of flourishing or being made whole, which enriches the common English gloss of 'healthy' or 'sound' by emphasizing progressive restoration and vitality.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ὑγιής is consistently translated as 'whole' or 'sound,' appearing 14 times and primarily conveying physical health or integrity, as seen in 12 occurrences translated simply as 'whole.' The word also carries a figurative meaning related to doctrinal truth, indicating something that is 'true' or 'healthy' in a spiritual or moral sense. This dual usage highlights the word's flexibility to describe both bodily health and soundness in teaching or belief, revealing a holistic concept of well-being in biblical thought.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ὑγιής underscores the biblical vision of restoration and completeness that God desires for His people. It points beyond mere physical healing to the wholeness of body, mind, and doctrine, reflecting the fullness of life in Christ. Recognizing ὑγιής as growth toward soundness invites believers to pursue spiritual maturity and doctrinal purity as integral to their health in God. This word reminds us that salvation and sanctification involve being made whole—restored and growing in every dimension of our being through the power of the Gospel.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 12:13, Jesus commands the man to stretch out his hand, which is then restored 'whole, like as the other.' The use of ὑγιής here emphasizes not just the healing of the hand but its complete restoration to full function and soundness. This illustrates Jesus' power to bring not partial but full wholeness, symbolizing the comprehensive healing and restoration He offers to all who trust in Him.
